cards.front: Which hormones act through a Gs protein, adenylyl cyclase and cAMP?
cards.back: Pituitary **ACTH, TSH, FSH, LH** and **MSH**, and placental **hCG**. Hypothalamic **CRH** and **GHRH**. Calcium hormones **PTH** and **calcitonin**. **Glucagon**. **ADH at V2** receptors. **Beta-1 and beta-2** adrenergic receptors. cAMP activates **protein kinase A**.
cards.back_pt: **ACTH, TSH, FSH, LH** e **MSH** hipofisários, e **hCG** placentário. **CRH** e **GHRH** hipotalâmicos. Hormônios do cálcio **PTH** e **calcitonina**. **Glucagon**. **ADH nos receptores V2**. Receptores adrenérgicos **beta-1 e beta-2**. O AMPc ativa a **proteína quinase A**.

cards.front: Which hormones act through a Gq protein, phospholipase C, IP3 and DAG?
cards.back: Hypothalamic **GnRH** and **TRH**. **Oxytocin** and **ADH at V1** receptors. **Angiotensin II**. **Gastrin**. **Alpha-1** adrenergic and **histamine H1** receptors. IP3 releases **calcium** from the endoplasmic reticulum; DAG activates **protein kinase C**.
cards.back_pt: **GnRH** e **TRH** hipotalâmicos. **Ocitocina** e **ADH nos receptores V1**. **Angiotensina II**. **Gastrina**. Receptores **alfa-1** adrenérgicos e **H1** da histamina. O IP3 libera **cálcio** do retículo endoplasmático; o DAG ativa a **proteína quinase C**.

cards.front: Which hormones use a receptor with its own tyrosine kinase, and which use a receptor that recruits JAK?
cards.back: **Intrinsic tyrosine kinase**: **insulin**, **IGF-1** and growth factors (**EGF, PDGF, FGF**). **No kinase of its own, recruits JAK (JAK/STAT)**: **GH**, **prolactin**, **erythropoietin**, **thrombopoietin** and many cytokines.
cards.back_pt: **Tirosina-quinase intrínseca**: **insulina**, **IGF-1** e fatores de crescimento (**EGF, PDGF, FGF**). **Sem quinase própria, recruta JAK (JAK/STAT)**: **GH**, **prolactina**, **eritropoetina**, **trombopoetina** e muitas citocinas.

cards.front: Which hormones bind receptors inside the cell, and how do they act?
cards.back: Lipid-soluble hormones: **steroids** (cortisol, aldosterone, estrogen, progesterone, testosterone), **thyroid hormone (T3)** and **calcitriol**. The hormone-receptor complex binds **response elements on DNA** and changes **gene transcription**, so effects start slowly (hours).
cards.back_pt: Hormônios lipossolúveis: **esteroides** (cortisol, aldosterona, estrogênio, progesterona, testosterona), **hormônio tireoidiano (T3)** e **calcitriol**. O complexo hormônio-receptor liga-se a **elementos de resposta no DNA** e altera a **transcrição gênica**, por isso o efeito começa devagar (horas).

cards.front: What is the first and rate-limiting step of steroid hormone synthesis?
cards.back: **StAR** protein moves cholesterol from the outer to the **inner mitochondrial membrane**. There, **desmolase** (cholesterol side-chain cleavage enzyme) makes **pregnenolone**. **ACTH** stimulates this step in the adrenal cortex; **LH** stimulates it in the gonads.
cards.back_pt: A proteína **StAR** leva o colesterol da membrana mitocondrial externa para a **membrana mitocondrial interna**. Ali, a **desmolase** (enzima de clivagem da cadeia lateral do colesterol) forma **pregnenolona**. O **ACTH** estimula essa etapa no córtex adrenal; o **LH** a estimula nas gônadas.

cards.front: Map the adrenal pathways from pregnenolone to aldosterone and to cortisol.
cards.back: Pregnenolone → (**3β-HSD**) progesterone. **Aldosterone**: progesterone → (**21-hydroxylase**) 11-deoxycorticosterone → (**11β-hydroxylase**) corticosterone → (**aldosterone synthase**, zona glomerulosa) aldosterone. **Cortisol**: **17α-hydroxylase** first → 17-OH-progesterone → (21-hydroxylase) 11-deoxycortisol → (11β-hydroxylase) cortisol.
cards.back_pt: Pregnenolona → (**3β-HSD**) progesterona. **Aldosterona**: progesterona → (**21-hidroxilase**) 11-desoxicorticosterona → (**11β-hidroxilase**) corticosterona → (**aldosterona sintase**, zona glomerulosa) aldosterona. **Cortisol**: primeiro a **17α-hidroxilase** → 17-OH-progesterona → (21-hidroxilase) 11-desoxicortisol → (11β-hidroxilase) cortisol.

cards.front: Map the sex-steroid branch of steroid synthesis.
cards.back: **17,20-lyase** (same enzyme as 17α-hydroxylase) makes **DHEA** and **androstenedione**. Androstenedione → **testosterone**. **5α-reductase**: testosterone → **DHT**. **Aromatase**: testosterone → **estradiol** and androstenedione → **estrone** (ovarian granulosa cells, adipose tissue, placenta).
cards.back_pt: A **17,20-liase** (mesma enzima da 17α-hidroxilase) forma **DHEA** e **androstenediona**. Androstenediona → **testosterona**. **5α-redutase**: testosterona → **DHT**. **Aromatase**: testosterona → **estradiol** e androstenediona → **estrona** (células da granulosa ovariana, tecido adiposo, placenta).

cards.front: How do peptide hormones and steroid hormones differ in blood transport and half-life?
cards.back: **Peptides** are water-soluble: they circulate mostly **free** and have **short half-lives** (minutes). **Steroids** and **thyroid hormone** travel mostly **bound** to carrier proteins (**CBG**, **SHBG**, **TBG**, albumin), so they last longer. Only the **free fraction** is active.
cards.back_pt: Os **peptídeos** são hidrossolúveis: circulam em sua maioria **livres** e têm **meia-vida curta** (minutos). Os **esteroides** e o **hormônio tireoidiano** circulam em grande parte **ligados** a proteínas carreadoras (**CBG**, **SHBG**, **TBG**, albumina), por isso duram mais. Só a **fração livre** é ativa.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman had transsphenoidal surgery for a pituitary adenoma 2 days ago. She now passes large volumes of dilute urine and is very thirsty. Serum sodium is 149 mEq/L, and urine osmolality is 110 mOsm/kg. After a dose of desmopressin, her urine output falls and urine osmolality rises to 520 mOsm/kg. Which intracellular pathway in the collecting duct cells mediates this response?
choices: Gq protein, phospholipase C, IP3 and calcium
Receptor guanylyl cyclase and cGMP
Gs protein, adenylyl cyclase, cAMP and protein kinase A
Janus kinase (JAK) and STAT transcription factors
Intracellular receptor binding to DNA response elements
questions.explanation: This is **central diabetes insipidus** after pituitary surgery. Desmopressin acts on **V2 receptors** of collecting duct principal cells, which are coupled to **Gs**. cAMP activates **protein kinase A**, and aquaporin-2 channels move into the apical membrane, so water is reabsorbed. **V1 receptors** on vascular smooth muscle use **Gq**/IP3, but they mediate vasoconstriction, not water reabsorption.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **diabetes insípido central** após cirurgia hipofisária. A desmopressina atua nos **receptores V2** das células principais do ducto coletor, acoplados à **proteína Gs**. O AMPc ativa a **proteína quinase A**, e canais de aquaporina-2 são inseridos na membrana apical, permitindo a reabsorção de água. Os **receptores V1** do músculo liso vascular usam **Gq**/IP3, mas medeiam vasoconstrição, não reabsorção de água.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman is evaluated for fatigue. An 8 AM serum cortisol level is elevated. She has taken a combined oral contraceptive for 2 years. She has no weight gain, purple striae, easy bruising or muscle weakness. Blood pressure is 118/74 mm Hg, and fasting glucose is normal. A 24-hour urine free cortisol, a late-night salivary cortisol and the plasma ACTH level are all normal. Which mechanism best explains her elevated serum cortisol?
choices: ACTH secretion by a pituitary adenoma
Autonomous cortisol secretion by an adrenal adenoma
ACTH secretion by a small cell lung carcinoma
Chronic stress activating the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis
Increased hepatic synthesis of cortisol-binding globulin
questions.explanation: **Estrogen** makes the liver produce more **cortisol-binding globulin (CBG, transcortin)**. More cortisol is bound, so **total serum cortisol rises**, but **free cortisol** stays normal: urine free cortisol and late-night salivary cortisol are normal, and she has no signs of Cushing syndrome. A pituitary ACTH adenoma (Cushing disease) is the most tempting choice, but it raises free cortisol, so urine free cortisol and late-night salivary cortisol would be high and clinical signs would usually be present.
questions.explanation_pt: O **estrogênio** faz o fígado produzir mais **globulina ligadora de cortisol (CBG, transcortina)**. Mais cortisol fica ligado, então o **cortisol sérico total sobe**, mas o **cortisol livre** fica normal: o cortisol livre urinário e o cortisol salivar noturno são normais, e ela não tem sinais de síndrome de Cushing. O adenoma hipofisário secretor de ACTH (doença de Cushing) é a alternativa mais tentadora, mas eleva o cortisol livre; assim, o cortisol livre urinário e o cortisol salivar noturno estariam altos, e geralmente haveria sinais clínicos.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old man with metastatic prostate cancer started abiraterone, an inhibitor of 17α-hydroxylase and 17,20-lyase, 6 weeks ago. He stopped the prednisone prescribed with it because it caused insomnia. Today his blood pressure is 164/98 mm Hg (previously 128/80 mm Hg). He has mild ankle edema. Serum potassium is 3.1 mEq/L. Which set of hormone changes best explains his findings?
choices: Decreased ACTH, decreased 11-deoxycorticosterone, increased cortisol
Increased ACTH, increased 11-deoxycorticosterone, decreased cortisol
Increased ACTH, decreased 11-deoxycorticosterone, decreased cortisol
Decreased ACTH, increased 11-deoxycorticosterone, increased cortisol
Normal ACTH, normal 11-deoxycorticosterone, decreased testosterone only
questions.explanation: Blocking **17α-hydroxylase** stops the cortisol and androgen branches. **Cortisol falls**, so **ACTH rises**, and pregnenolone is pushed into the only open branch: **11-deoxycorticosterone** and corticosterone accumulate. 11-deoxycorticosterone is a **mineralocorticoid**, so it causes hypertension, edema and **hypokalemia**; prednisone is given to suppress ACTH. A **21-hydroxylase** block also raises ACTH and lowers cortisol, but it lowers 11-deoxycorticosterone and causes salt loss, not hypertension.
questions.explanation_pt: O bloqueio da **17α-hidroxilase** interrompe os ramos do cortisol e dos andrógenos. O **cortisol cai**, então o **ACTH sobe**, e a pregnenolona é desviada para o único ramo aberto: acumulam-se **11-desoxicorticosterona** e corticosterona. A 11-desoxicorticosterona é um **mineralocorticoide**, por isso causa hipertensão, edema e **hipocalemia**; a prednisona é usada para suprimir o ACTH. O bloqueio da **21-hidroxilase** também eleva o ACTH e reduz o cortisol, mas reduz a 11-desoxicorticosterona e causa perda de sal, e não hipertensão.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man has noticed over several years that his rings and shoes no longer fit. He has a large jaw, wide spaces between his lower teeth, coarse facial features, and large, sweaty hands. Serum IGF-1 is elevated. MRI shows a 1.6-cm pituitary mass. The hormone made by this tumor acts on hepatocytes to stimulate IGF-1 production. Which type of receptor does this hormone bind on hepatocytes?
choices: Receptor with intrinsic tyrosine kinase activity
Receptor coupled to a Gs protein
Receptor coupled to a Gq protein
Cytokine-type receptor that recruits JAK kinases
Intracellular receptor that binds DNA
questions.explanation: This is **acromegaly** from a **GH-secreting pituitary adenoma**. The **GH receptor** has no kinase activity of its own; it belongs to the **cytokine receptor** family and signals through **JAK/STAT**, which drives hepatic **IGF-1** production. The most tempting wrong answer is the intrinsic tyrosine kinase receptor: that is the receptor for **IGF-1** (and insulin), which mediates many growth effects of GH, but not for GH itself.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **acromegalia** por **adenoma hipofisário secretor de GH**. O **receptor de GH** não tem atividade quinase própria; pertence à família dos **receptores de citocinas** e sinaliza via **JAK/STAT**, estimulando a produção hepática de **IGF-1**. A alternativa mais tentadora é o receptor com tirosina-quinase intrínseca: é o receptor do **IGF-1** (e da insulina), que medeia muitos efeitos de crescimento do GH, mas não o do próprio GH.

notes.title: Hormone signaling, steroid synthesis, transport and appetite
notes.body_md:
## Receptor types

- **Gs → cAMP → PKA**: ACTH, TSH, FSH, LH, hCG, MSH, CRH, GHRH, PTH, calcitonin, glucagon, ADH (V2), beta-1 and beta-2.
- **Gq → IP3/DAG → calcium and PKC**: GnRH, TRH, oxytocin, ADH (V1), angiotensin II, gastrin, alpha-1, H1.
- **Intrinsic tyrosine kinase**: insulin, IGF-1, EGF, PDGF, FGF.
- **JAK/STAT** (cytokine receptors): GH, prolactin, erythropoietin, thrombopoietin.
- **cGMP**: **ANP/BNP** (membrane guanylyl cyclase) and **nitric oxide** (soluble guanylyl cyclase).
- **Intracellular receptors**: steroids, T3 and calcitriol change gene transcription.

## Steroid synthesis

- **StAR** brings cholesterol into the mitochondria; **desmolase** turns it into **pregnenolone**. This is the rate-limiting step.
- Without **17α-hydroxylase**: mineralocorticoids (the only branch in the zona glomerulosa).
- With 17α-hydroxylase: cortisol (**21-** then **11β-hydroxylase**) or androgens (**17,20-lyase**).
- **Aromatase** turns androgens into estrogens; **5α-reductase** turns testosterone into DHT.

## Transport

- **Peptides** dissolve in plasma, act on membrane receptors and have short half-lives.
- **Steroids** and **thyroid hormone** travel mostly bound (**TBG**, **SHBG**, **CBG**, albumin), so they last longer.
- Only the **free** hormone is active.
- **Estrogen** (pregnancy, oral contraceptives) raises binding proteins: total levels rise, free levels stay normal.

## Feedback

- **Long loop**: the target hormone (cortisol, T4) inhibits the hypothalamus and pituitary.
- **Short loop**: a pituitary hormone inhibits its own releasing hormone.
- **Positive feedback**: high, sustained estradiol before ovulation triggers the **LH surge**.
- **IGF-1** from the liver carries out most growth effects of GH and feeds back to reduce GH.

## Appetite

- **Leptin** from fat cells signals satiety; **ghrelin** from the stomach signals hunger.
- **Lateral hypothalamus**: hunger center; damage causes anorexia.
- **Ventromedial hypothalamus**: satiety center; damage causes overeating and obesity.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Tipos de receptor

- **Gs → AMPc → PKA**: ACTH, TSH, FSH, LH, hCG, MSH, CRH, GHRH, PTH, calcitonina, glucagon, ADH (V2), beta-1 e beta-2.
- **Gq → IP3/DAG → cálcio e PKC**: GnRH, TRH, ocitocina, ADH (V1), angiotensina II, gastrina, alfa-1, H1.
- **Tirosina-quinase intrínseca**: insulina, IGF-1, EGF, PDGF, FGF.
- **JAK/STAT** (receptores de citocinas): GH, prolactina, eritropoetina, trombopoetina.
- **GMPc**: **ANP/BNP** (guanilato ciclase de membrana) e **óxido nítrico** (guanilato ciclase solúvel).
- **Receptores intracelulares**: esteroides, T3 e calcitriol alteram a transcrição gênica.

## Síntese de esteroides

- A **StAR** leva o colesterol para a mitocôndria; a **desmolase** o transforma em **pregnenolona**. Essa é a etapa limitante.
- Sem **17α-hidroxilase**: mineralocorticoides (o único ramo na zona glomerulosa).
- Com 17α-hidroxilase: cortisol (**21-** e depois **11β-hidroxilase**) ou andrógenos (**17,20-liase**).
- A **aromatase** transforma andrógenos em estrogênios; a **5α-redutase** transforma testosterona em DHT.

## Transporte

- **Peptídeos** se dissolvem no plasma, agem em receptores de membrana e têm meia-vida curta.
- **Esteroides** e **hormônio tireoidiano** circulam em grande parte ligados (**TBG**, **SHBG**, **CBG**, albumina), por isso duram mais.
- Só o hormônio **livre** é ativo.
- O **estrogênio** (gestação, anticoncepcionais orais) aumenta as proteínas ligadoras: os níveis totais sobem, e os livres ficam normais.

## *Feedback*

- **Alça longa**: o hormônio-alvo (cortisol, T4) inibe o hipotálamo e a hipófise.
- **Alça curta**: um hormônio hipofisário inibe o seu próprio hormônio liberador.
- ***Feedback* positivo**: estradiol alto e sustentado antes da ovulação desencadeia o **pico de LH**.
- O **IGF-1** hepático executa a maior parte dos efeitos de crescimento do GH e inibe a secreção de GH.

## Apetite

- A **leptina** dos adipócitos sinaliza saciedade; a **grelina** do estômago sinaliza fome.
- **Hipotálamo lateral**: centro da fome; lesão causa anorexia.
- **Hipotálamo ventromedial**: centro da saciedade; lesão causa hiperfagia e obesidade.
